task_spec: subject: reconstruct playlists in a base Traktor NML from a source (older) NML - where the base holds playlist names whose contents diverge from the source, fill the base playlist in place from the union of both, instead of importing a renamed '<name> (2)' duplicate
scope: C:/codex/traktor-nml-tool - traktor_nml/splice.py, traktor_nml/playlists.py, traktor_nml/commands/splice_cmd.py, tests/test_splice.py

MUST: a reconstructed playlist must NOT also be appended as an imported '<name> (2)' duplicate (current half-finished state does exactly this)
MUST: base file is never rewritten in place; output is a separate full copy - already true of splice, must stay true
MUST: base playlist keeps its own NODE, UUID and folder position when filled

current_understanding: splice merges a base NML with further NMLs: base is authoritative for its own COLLECTION and playlists and its bytes are never rewritten; track identity across inputs uses record_keys tier ordering cascaded through union-find

playlist import APPENDS each incoming playlist into base's root SUBNODES as a fragment; base's SUBNODES span is otherwise copied verbatim - so filling a base playlist means replacing a span INSIDE that verbatim region, which the existing assembly has no path for

the uncommitted pre-pass works around this by rewriting base_source (replacements applied end-first so offsets stay valid), re-parsing base_root via xmlio.parse_xml_bytes, then letting the existing assembly run on the rewritten text

measured state of the half-finished work: base MySet correctly filled 0 -> 2 entries in place, stats playlists_reconstructed=1, BUT playlists_imported=1 and playlists_renamed=1 as well, so the output still carries a redundant 'MySet (2)'. That exclusion is the known missing piece

ambiguity is an existing first-class outcome in matching.py:match_records (a tier matching more than one candidate); splice already aborts on unresolved identity conflicts and writes its conflict report either way (DL-008)
an incoming PRIMARYKEY with no old_to_new_key entry and no base counterpart already becomes an unresolved_reference, which assemble_output aborts on at the end
tests/test_splice.py currently passes 7/7 with the uncommitted pre-pass present and the flag off
assumptions: content comparison should compare the REDIRECTED key sequence, not raw source keys, since base and source name the same track by different keys (H)

order-sensitive comparison: a reordered but otherwise identical playlist counts as 'differs' and triggers a combine, which is a no-op on membership but rewrites order to base-first (M) - worth confirming with the user
'ambiguous' here means one incoming key whose identity group holds more than one base record, so no single base key is the right redirect target (M)
the ambiguity report should follow splice_cmd.py's existing _write_conflict_report CSV convention (csv.DictWriter, newline='', UTF-8) rather than a second dialect (H)
the wizard step is wanted after the CLI works, not simultaneously (H - user said 'then the GUI step')
playlist_entry_count becomes unused once the count trigger is removed and should be deleted rather than left dead (M)
invisible_knowledge: DL-007: byte-span assembly (splice/split) and attribute-patching writes (rewrite/reconnect) must never mix within one command; splice is span-assembly, so reconstruction must stay on the span path and must not route through write_nml_safely
DL-008: an unresolved conflict aborts the whole write, and the report is written either way - the convention the ambiguity check must reproduce rather than inventing a second failure shape

DL-029: a same-name collision takes a deterministic '<name> (2)' rename with a freshly generated UUID, because two PLAYLIST elements sharing one UUID within a file is invalid. Reconstruction deliberately departs from this for the matched-name case, which is why it needs its own decision-log entry

DL-037: build-playlist keeps duplicate entries from duplicate input lines because a Traktor PLAYLIST is an ordered list of references, not a set, and the operator authored those lines. Reconstruction dedupes instead - the duplication there would be an artefact of merging two documents, not authored input. The two policies must each state why

fragments that no rename or redirect touched are transplanted as verbatim source byte spans; only renamed playlists and redirected PRIMARYKEY values are re-serialised - a reconstructed playlist is necessarily re-serialised
the ENTRIES attribute on a PLAYLIST is the value a reconstruction recalculates, so it must not be trusted as the input to deciding whether to reconstruct

Traktor's tolerance of a playlist carrying a UUID other than the one it shipped with is confirmed only by manual Traktor import, not by the test suite (package log R-004) - filling base's node in place avoids opening a second unverified case, since base keeps its own UUID

the user's real-world use case is the critical one for this tool: playlists in a current collection are blank, and a previous collection holds their contents; path repair matters because the two collections reference tracks at different locations
